premises.text: Existing voice apps fail because they miss popular apps and limit voice to only a few apps
premises.evidence_span: they don't work with the most popular apps out there. And the second is, they limit their technology to only a few apps

premises.text: VoiceSphere works with many of the most popular consumer apps from the start inside one feed without leaving the app
premises.evidence_span: VoiceSphere works with 20 of the most popular apps right from the start

premises.text: An API hub lets new apps be integrated quickly with only a few lines of code
premises.evidence_span: the API hub is really advanced technology that allows us to integrate more and more apps really fast

premises.text: Professionals can voice-access complex business software such as Salesforce inside VoiceSphere
premises.evidence_span: professionals could reach all the data and functionality of these products just with their voice

premises.text: An enterprise store lets business products with APIs sell VoiceSphere integrations while VoiceSphere takes a share of each sale
premises.evidence_span: They can integrate their application and sell the VoiceSphere access to their customers inside our enterprise store

value.text: Users can talk to all their favorite apps and complex software by voice
value.evidence_span: a voice control app that lets you talk to all your favorite apps

causal_links.evidence_span: what makes VoiceSphere really stand apart is how easy it is to integrate new products in VoiceSphere
VoiceSphere, the app that lets you talk to everything on your phone
allows us to integrate more and more apps really fast
lets complex software benefit from our technology

notes: Two voice-control problems coded as one pain-bundle (P1) per v1.5.1 §4.1. Cross-service Spotify/YouTube fallback folded into P2 as cascade of the popular-apps mechanism. Singleton D2 retained: API hub is independently revisable extensibility. 20% take rate kept as quantitative detail of P5.
